name: dispatch-guard
description: Enforces a sub-task dispatch protocol and brakes on usage limits. One sub-task at a time unless the owner approves a count; the plan and every sub-task prompt land on disk before any dispatch; and dispatching is refused outright once the usage window is nearly spent. Also ships the unattended-work skill (how to work for a long stretch with nobody watching) and the cowork skill (several sessions sharing one working tree for one owner), two of whose rules the hook enforces: an append-only record may only grow, and a session sharing a tree with a live peer loads the skill before it writes. Needs Claude Code 2.0.56 or later: earlier builds do not know the PostToolUseFailure event this plugin subscribes to, and one unknown event silences every hook of the plugin.

announce_unattended_work.title: Remind every session to load the unattended-work skill
announce_unattended_work.description: On by default. Turn it off to keep the skill installed but invoke it yourself. It cannot disable the hook - a plugin's hooks always fire - so what it switches off is what the hook PRINTS.
